findings.title: A policy waiver of any rule some scan enforces non-canonically is now a hard error, including where that rule is canonical elsewhere or the target is not *
locations: src/CLI/Doctor.jl:343-346 CFG.EXEMPTIONS (the new FAIL, in QUICK)
test/scans.jl:187-203 (the base assertion that a RULE.CIT.DOI waiver disables the scan flipped to @test_throws)
findings.after:
for rule in rules_for_scan(id)
        rule == canonical && continue
        e = first(Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy"), 1)
        isempty(e) || throw(Ledger.LedgerError("$rule on $(e[1]["target"]) is a policy waiver of a rule $id enforces but " * ...
findings.why_it_matters: Previously valid input: a ledger entry `id = "RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING"`, `scope = "policy"`, `target = "*"`. At rc.11 it disabled SCAN.HTML_DOCSTRING_ONCE, SCAN.HTML_PUBLIC_HOME and SCAN.HTML_BASE_LEAK, whose canonical rule it is; at base it also disabled SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE. Now unreachable_waiver_scans returns ["SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE"], so CFG.EXEMPTIONS FAILs. That check is in QUICK, so the consumer's Pkg.test() (TestHarness.gate), its docs build (makedocs runs doctor QUICK) and every preflight refuse. And `gbg scan docs` crashes with exit 3, because the LedgerError escapes run_scan. The same holds for a narrowly targeted entry the ledger guide still documents, e.g. RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE on one file. Before, that entry was never a disable in the engine, so it was never 'silently wide'; its rule also carries `panel`, which the waiver legitimately reaches. The one remedy offered, `scope = "scan"` on SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE, withdraws RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API as well, the very widening the refusal says it prevents. A package deviating from the API-grouping rule, or waiving the inaccessible-source rule for one page, can no longer write that deviation and has its test and docs gates broken until it deletes it.
findings.description: The defect was a target-* waiver of a scan's second rule silently disabling the scan's canonical rule too. The fix is wider in three ways. (1) It refuses the waiver for EVERY scan the rule reaches, even where the rule is canonical for other scans: RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING owns three HTML scans and is only a second rule of SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE. (2) It refuses entries of any target and any match table, although only target '*' ever disabled anything. (3) It raises in the scan engine and in a QUICK doctor check, so the refusal fails the consumer's test and docs gates instead of warning. A narrower fix would ignore a non-canonical waiver in the engine and WARN when the rule is canonical nowhere, or refuse only target-* entries on rules with no canonical scan. The same window also rewrote the test oracle that asserted the base behaviour.
findings.evidence: catalog/scans.toml: `id = "SCAN.HTML_DOCSTRING_ONCE" rule = "RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING"` (likewise HTML_PUBLIC_HOME, HTML_BASE_LEAK); RULES.toml RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING `check = ["scan:SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE", "scan:SCAN.HTML_DOCSTRING_ONCE", ...]`; RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE `check = ["scan:SCAN.DEAD_REF", "panel"]`; Doctor.jl `const QUICK = [..., "CFG.EXEMPTIONS", ...]`; ledger.md `target = "*"  # or a symbol, a file, a glob, a finding id` and 'An optional [exemption.match] table ... refines a scan, lint, policy or harness entry'; test diff `- @test isempty(r.hits) && r.exempted > 0  # the waiver that was void` → `+ @test_throws G.Ledger.LedgerError G.run_scan(d, row; ledger = pol(second))`; v1.0.0-rc.11 apply_ledger: `for e in Ledger.entries(ledger, rule; scope = "policy") e["target"] == "*" && return ...` (no throw)

findings.title: A git root with no HEAD is newly refused by round build and round scripts, and scripts refuses only after it has already replaced the frozen copies
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:408-417 refresh_scripts (install_script loop, then the RoundError)
src/CLI/Preflight.jl:952 (a round still opens with head = "0"^40 on such a root)
findings.before:
code = run_under_round(cfg, round, cfg["package"]["docs_build"]; log)
    rec["build"] = Dict{String,Any}("code" => code, "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40), ...)  /  entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))
findings.after: Git.head(cfg["root"]) === nothing && (println(io, "build: refused — the root has no git HEAD, so no build here can be recorded as current"); return 2)  /  Preflight.install_script(src, dst) ... head === nothing && throw(RoundError("scripts: the root has no git HEAD to record the refresh against"))
findings.why_it_matters: Previously valid input: `gbg round build <round>` and `gbg round scripts <round>` on a round that preflight opened in a repository with no commit yet. Preflight still allows that, recording head 0^40. `build` used to run the consumer's docs build under GBG_ROUND, the only sanctioned way to build while a round is open, and now builds nothing (exit 2), though `prepare` and `pass open` still build in the same state and merely skip the record. `scripts` now overwrites the round's frozen Workflow copies and then throws, so the refresh happens and is NOT recorded in ROUND.toml. That is the untraced hand refresh this verb and its new schema fields exist to prevent.
findings.description: Refusing a placeholder head so that close cannot be satisfied by an uncheckable build is defensible for the RECORD. The edit is wider than that: `build` stops building rather than building unrecorded, as its siblings do. The check in `refresh_scripts` also sits after the mutation instead of beside the reason check at the top, so the new rejection leaves the round in the unrecorded state.
findings.evidence: Rounds.jl refresh_scripts: `for (name, src) in Preflight.script_sources(...) ... Preflight.install_script(src, dst) end` then `isempty(moved) && ...` then `head === nothing && throw(RoundError(...))`; Passes.jl pass_open: `why = Rounds.record_build!(cfg, dir, rec, code); why === nothing || println(io, "pass open: the build is NOT RECORDED — $why")` (continues); Preflight.jl:952 `head = something(Git.head(root), "0"^40)`

findings.title: gbg round scripts <round>, the base form, is now refused without --reason, and the CLI usage line still omits the flag
locations: test/rounds.jl:859-861 (the base call `refresh_scripts(cfg, name)` rewritten to require a reason)
findings.before: `gbg round scripts <round>`: re-copies this round's Workflow scripts from the instrument, and records that it happened. ... function refresh_scripts(cfg::AbstractDict, round::AbstractString; io::IO = stdout)
findings.after: length(strip(reason)) >= 24 || (println(io, "scripts: refused — --reason \"…\" (≥ 24 characters) must say why this round's frozen scripts cannot serve it"); return 2)
findings.why_it_matters: Previously valid input: `gbg round scripts 2026-..-check-docs-01`, the form base documented in the docstring and in the round schema. It now exits 2. A session following the CLI's own usage text (`gbg round prepare|build|test|scripts|... <round>`) is refused without being told the flag exists until it runs the verb. Exposure is limited: the verb is in no tag (6bf4571 is contained by none), so only dev-checkout rounds are affected.
findings.description: Requiring a recorded reason makes a mid-round script change visible, and the same window rewrote RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND to admit exactly that. The rejection is proportionate in spirit. It goes past the defect in two small ways: the length floor of 24 differs from the 12 that `import --empty` and `--rebaseline` ask for, and the usage string, the first place a caller looks, was not updated.
findings.evidence: usage at head: `usage: gbg round prepare|build|test|scripts|bank|rerun|grade|close|abandon|list|render <round> | ...`; base schema: "each time `gbg round scripts <round>` re-copied this round's Workflow scripts"; `git tag --contains 6bf4571` → empty

findings.title: A ROUND.toml written by the base scripts verb no longer validates, making its round unloadable and every gate fatal
locations: schema/round.schema.json:240-290 scripts_refreshed items (required reason, after_pass, scripts)
findings.why_it_matters: Previously valid input: a round record holding `scripts_refreshed = [{at, head}]`, exactly what base's `gbg round scripts` wrote. Under head, RoundFiles.read_round rejects it. Every round verb on that round exits 2 (cannot evaluate), including abandon and close, and gate_problems marks it :invalid and fatal, so that consumer's Pkg.test() and docs build refuse until someone hand-edits a file stamped 'never edited by hand'. No schema_version moves. The exposure is dev-only, since the verb was never tagged, and the tool's own tests pass, which suggests no such record exists here.
findings.description: Making the new fields required for new refreshes is the change's purpose. Applying the requirement to entries the previous writer produced, with no default and no migration, turns a record the tool itself wrote into a fatal gate error. Required-for-new with optional-for-old, or a schema_version step, would have been the narrow form.
findings.evidence: Gate.jl: `if r.state in (:nomarker, :invalid) println(io, "gate: round directory $(r.name) has no valid ROUND.toml — exit 2"); fatal = true`; RoundFiles.read_round: `isempty(errs) || error("$(p) is invalid:...")`; base Rounds.jl: `entry = Dict{String,Any}("at" => timestamp(), "head" => something(Git.head(cfg["root"]), "0"^40))`

findings.title: AUDIT.GAP now warns when an audit's base equals the previous closed head but that commit is unreachable
findings.after:
(!isempty(base) && Git.is_ancestor(ctx.root, base, prev)) ||
            push!(gaps, "... is not ...'s closed head ... or an ancestor of it — the commits between were never audited")
findings.why_it_matters: Previously valid input: two contiguous closed audits, base exactly equal to the earlier closed_head, in a checkout where that commit is absent (a shallow CI clone, or history rewritten after both closed). Equality passed it. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails on a missing object, so the check now WARNs with a message claiming commits went unaudited, which is false for an exact match. It is a WARN in QUICK, so no gate fails, but it runs in every makedocs and Pkg.test.
findings.description: Widening equality to ancestry was the stated fix, for overlaps. Dropping the exact-equality short-circuit is extra, and it reclassifies a contiguous pair as a gap whenever the commit cannot be resolved. `base == prev ||` ahead of the ancestry test would keep the fix without the new warning.
findings.evidence: Doctor.jl head: `prev = String(get(audits[i-1].round, "closed_head", audits[i-1].round["head"])); base = String(get(audits[i].round, "base", "")); (!isempty(base) && Git.is_ancestor(ctx.root, base, prev)) || push!(gaps, ...)`; ARCHITECTURE §12.C row now reads 'otherwise, or unreachable (WARN)'
